title: Why Is This Harp Seal the Worst Mother?
negative_prompt: people, human equipment, text, letters, numbers, watermark, logo, cartoon, anime, tears, duplicate seals, extra limbs, deformed anatomy, adult markings on a white pup, newborn coat after the juvenile moult, fabricated rescue

worlds.base_prompt: Warm, lively painterly natural-history illustration with expressive composition but anatomically accurate true seals; crisp subject silhouettes, bright ivory ice and teal water, gold reserved for explanatory energy graphics. The same mother and pup across shots. Adult mother: silver-gray coat, dark face and characteristic curved saddle marking; no harbor-seal look. Young pup: white lanugo, short flippers, no external ears. Later juvenile: gray-spotted coat, explicitly later chronology. Center all critical action inside the middle 70 percent of a 9:16 composition. No text, no logos, no humans or props, no open wounds. Use a reference image for identity and palette, not to copy its pose or developmental age. Adult harp seal: streamlined silver-gray body with natural dark markings and short foreflippers. Newborn/young pup: compact body in a white lanugo coat during nursing. Older juvenile after moulting: gray-spotted coat, still juvenile proportions. Never draw human-like limbs, hands, tears, clothing, collars, or adult saddle markings on a young pup.

narration.narration: Why is this harp seal the worst mother? After about twelve days, she leaves. Her pup cannot feed itself yet.
Dinner service: closed. But there is food hidden in this pup.
Before she left, Mom's rich milk built a thick layer of fat. A built-in lunchbox.
After weaning, that stored energy fuels the pup for weeks without meals.
But there is a catch. It still needs ice to rest on as it develops. Break that up too soon, and young pups can drown.
Mom leaves the fuel. The ice has to last.

evidence.claim: NOAA reports about 12 days of high-fat nursing, rapid daily weight gain, blubber development, then a post-weaning period on the ice without eating before independent feeding.
evidence.qualification: Use about; do not imply every gram of growth is fat.
evidence.license: Publicly accessible government factual source; summarized, not quoted

evidence.claim: DFO reports pups are nursed for about 12 days, gain more than 2.2 kg per day, and females leave the ice after the pups are weaned.
evidence.qualification: Female mating after departure is factual but omitted because it does not answer the pup food-gap question.
evidence.license: Publicly accessible government factual source; summarized, not quoted

evidence.claim: DFO reports young harp seals need stable ice for nursing and post-weaning resting; storms can break poor ice and force young seals into water where they can drown.
evidence.qualification: Say can, not that every pup drowns or that entering water itself is always fatal.
evidence.license: Publicly accessible government factual source; summarized, not quoted

prohibited_claims: Do not imply that the mother intends cruelty, returns after weaning, or guarantees survival.
A conditional ice-risk illustration is not the observed death of this individual.
Lunchbox is a metaphor for stored body fat, not a literal human object.

nature_short.voice_instructions: A bright, curious, playful science storyteller speaking to one friend. Natural American English, forward momentum around 175-185 words per minute, clear consonants and a smile on the dinner-service and lunchbox lines. Start immediately. Make the opening question skeptical rather than angry. Punch LEAVES, FOOD, FAT and ICE once, without shouting. Give the hidden-food reveal a tiny anticipatory pause. Turn serious for the conditional ice risk, then land the final line decisively. No announcer voice, no sleepy documentary cadence, no dramatic gasp, no extra words. Do not read these directions aloud.
